harbor_p26_001.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_001.text: By the middle of the private week, Yue had learned which footsteps belonged to the lodging keeper and no longer mistook each knock for an overdue task. She paid for ordinary meals from her own purse and spent one morning doing nothing more ambitious than mending her bedding's torn corner. The habitual cloth would travel with her. At the window she saw Fen crossing toward the account shop with her private learning book, while Luo walked another road carrying a light ordinary work basket. Their separate directions looked less frightening from above than they had sounded over supper.

harbor_p26_002.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_002.text: Han came at the agreed private hour with a question about the final selection meeting. The council wanted Yue's comparison of the three eligible plans presented once, then a recommendation under its authorized process. The accepting keeper and fiscal clerk would countersign the selected plan after the ordinary committee confirmed it. Her former stage and appointment supplied no independent right to spend. She could decline the voluntary presentation. Yue agreed to that bounded final role, unpaid and limited to the observed comparison she actually knew. Han gave her the public agenda and kept protected office files at their desk.

harbor_p26_003.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_003.text: The agenda called the last item the harbor's continuing arrangement. Yue disliked the phrase because it sounded larger than one sixty-four pilot. Han brought the concern to the council clerk, who amended the public heading to a bounded pilot selection. Existing rights and ordinary duties remained outside that item. The clerk smiled tiredly and asked whether final weeks made every adjective dangerous. Han said only the ambitious ones. They laughed. Yue stood nearby with her personal cup, surprised at how little ceremony remained once the actual task fit its name. A recommendation could still change what people received next month.

harbor_p26_004.speaker: harbor_sui_yan
harbor_p26_004.text: I will present the repair plan's technical source and current independent role limits. Han can explain registry custody and hours, and the route lead can answer the road schedule. Yue can compare the observations she actually made and identify the other staff accounts. Then the committee can confirm one recommendation within the reservation already approved. No keeper should be surprised by a duty she supposedly accepted. I have checked mine. I would like every question about launch work answered before the room starts asking which drawing looks more hopeful. Hope is a poor substitute for knowing who has the key.

harbor_p26_005.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_005.text: The registry keeper's launch schedule named the staff who could perform the bounded receiving and indexing work within twenty-four copper. Its translation task had agreed providers, language scope and sixteen payment after checked completion. The cabinet and forms would cost twelve each under the accepted quotes. The proposed launch work could occur during the final private days if selected, followed by the ordinary desk's later reviews at four and eight weeks. Han showed the named cover for her leave intervals. Her private painting would not disappear because the cabinet acquired a label, nor would it become the fund's unpriced decoration.

harbor_p26_006.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_006.text: The repair keeper's launch plan used the twenty-eight cover and fitting quote already checked, sixteen for ordinary inspections, twelve for crew-report instruction and eight for the bounded post-installation follow-up. The later four- and eight-week reviews belonged to the accepted ordinary technical role, not a secret promise of more visitor labor. Yan would perform only the part allowed by his current result; independent signoff stayed with the assigned officer. The sample and tools came from the port under their task arrangements. Sui asked the carpenter about the first stuck fastening again, receiving the corrected measurement rather than reassuring praise.

harbor_p26_007.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_007.text: The road keeper confirmed four six-copper return journeys within twenty-four, with the actual workers and collection hours accepted. Two collection visits and two reply visits could be made during two safe launch days if selected, one worker per paid fare. Interpretation twelve, protected forms twelve and staff time sixteen completed the sixty-four. The current licensed inner route allowed the schedule; an unsafe change would postpone travel with a real status, not demand courage from a ticket. Rong had accepted the corrected hour. Yue listened to the plan without imagining her body divided between every boat and receiving room.

harbor_p26_008.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_008.text: At the public preparation table, Li Su asked whether the registry's written explanation still used large clear words. Han showed the actual form sample and its scope. Li read it while another worker asked the route lead about missing a collection hour. The keeper gave the existing alternative and the selected pilot's bounded schedule. Deren examined the repair drawing with his independent explainer. These were different kinds of use, not three ways to prove the same person morally better. Yue watched actual questions fit or fail against actual details and felt her own preference change twice before the kettle cooled.

harbor_p26_009.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_009.text: He Ming came after the packing interval, carrying no business account for the public fund. She wanted road visits and asked the other two proposers to say honestly what would remain unavailable if their plan won. The registry would not staff a permanent reader across the water. The repair plan would not translate a household letter. The road would not add cover fittings or create an evening index cabinet. Ordinary existing services and duties would continue, with their current limits. He Ming said she preferred the road even after hearing the omissions.

harbor_p26_010.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_010.text: An accompanied her for the public discussion and kept his recent investment embarrassment private. He wanted the registry now, because customers could find receiving routes near their work and because his sister read poorly after a long shift. Zhou still liked repair. Ke wanted the place she could reach without leaving paid hours. Wu gave the canteen's actual closing time and favored the road's later reply visit if it fit. The group disagreed without making the larger packing room a vote it had to deliver together. Their venture already had enough real decisions to make without annexing everybody's public opinion.

harbor_p26_011.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_011.text: Deren asked Yan privately whether the foreman favored repair because it would make his own signoff easier to regain. Yan said the fitting might help a particular check and could not replace the result's independent conditions. He favored it because hidden support had mattered. Then he asked whether Deren wanted him to stop defending the plan so the injured man could claim it alone. Deren stared and laughed. He said that sounded like a new species of foolish generosity. They argued for the same plan and still differed about why.

harbor_p26_012.speaker: harbor_yan_su
harbor_p26_012.text: I am trying to avoid turning every opinion into a request that you forgive me. Apparently that effort has now acquired its errors. Tell me when I do it. I can want a better fitting and still carry the missed check. I can also eat supper with you without offering to carry your cup as a gesture of repentance. The cup looks heavy enough to require a crew. If repair wins, we will do the work under the roles. If it loses, the port still owes the checks already required. I have read that clause until the letters look exhausted.

harbor_p26_013.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_013.text: Deren said the cup would nominate itself as fiscal keeper if allowed. Bo overheard and asked whether pottery could claim extra shifts. Yan told him to finish the ordinary kit count, then admitted the joke was better than his last three. The young rigger looked absurdly pleased. They returned to the day's actual load task within the known role boundaries. Yue watched from the public side only briefly, then went to meet Fen at the shop's agreed closing hour. Her private week still contained people whose ambitions had nothing to do with the committee's sixty-four.

harbor_p26_014.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_014.text: Fen wanted to visit the cart stand where her father's departure would begin after the final checks. Luo agreed, and the three went outside the loading boundary to read the licensed route notice. The ticket matched the accepted light-work start and travel interval. There was no sudden heroic need to leave tonight. Fen studied the step and said it looked offensively normal for something that had frightened her so much. Luo said the first one had looked normal too. They stood together while a passenger boarded, then went to buy private tea instead of rehearsing grief at the empty road.

harbor_p26_015.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_015.text: At tea, Fen asked whether her father would write that he was well even when he was not. Luo admitted he might be tempted and promised the contact they agreed would not depend on pretending every week good. He did not promise to disclose private thoughts. She wanted warning if injury or work changed the agreed plan, and he accepted that. Yue listened, then asked Fen about the apprenticeship skill. The girl described a column with excitement before remembering the cart. Both subjects belonged to her. Her father smiled as if the shift between them had become bearable to watch.

harbor_p26_016.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_016.text: Aning joined afterward with the aunt's permitted finish time already met. She asked why everyone looked solemn at a stall that sold such unserious buns. Fen said her father was preparing to leave and adults insisted the fare had meaning. Aning said fares mainly meant less money afterward. The joke made Luo laugh. The girls argued about the cheapest filling while Yue bought her own portion. They went home by the ordinary clear road, letting tomorrow's work remain tomorrow. The future had not become certain, and supper could still be chosen through appetite rather than fear.

harbor_p26_017.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_017.text: At the renewed room, Han moved her painting board to catch better light. Yue helped carry only the light stand when asked, with hands and no new tool acquisition. The kite-common picture now had another figure added near the wall. Han said it was Qin, though the figure looked like a cabbage with spectacles. Yue admired the resemblance and received a swat from the clerk's cloth. They laughed, then sat to discuss the first road reply. A next address still did not exist. They would wait until Yue could share one rather than invent a household she had never visited.

harbor_p26_018.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_018.text: Han asked whether the traveler would carry her name into every new place. Yue said she would remember it and disliked making memory sound like ownership. The clerk said she had asked for something simpler: whether she would think of the room. Yue answered yes. They sat quietly until Han asked if that had been difficult to say. It had. The traveler was better at accounts than at affection when no term could protect it. Han took her hand and said the answer had worked without a form. The cup beside them cooled while neither reached to improve the moment.

harbor_p26_019.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_019.text: The lodging keeper brought a fare list for the ordinary onward cart and connecting ferry, at Yue's request. She would choose after the final selection and route check, paying from her own earned purse. No captain promised passage at public expense. The source named the actual carrier and times, without guaranteeing weather six weeks ahead. Yue wanted the road open and the private week longer. Both desires could remain while she read. She kept the public fare reference in personal travel papers and returned the borrowed list. The habitual pack required no harbor equipment to make a road possible.

harbor_p26_020.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_020.text: At Willow Reach, Jun's update reached He Ming under their private contact. Their mother had gone back to complaining about garden weeds, which pleased both children more than any dignified recovery message could. He Ming read the permitted family letter at home, not at the public table, and chose a contribution from her earned share for a need they had actually discussed. The partnership's reserve fourteen stayed its own. She would not make employees wait for wages because family affection happened to arrive with a bill. Later she told Wu the weeds sounded stronger than the hip, and both laughed.

harbor_p26_021.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_021.text: Wu's next canteen task proceeded at its stated hours. Her children stayed with the agreed keeper, and the duck remained in the household basket rather than become a visitor at work. She had acquired a stable rhythm imperfect enough to contain missed naps and loud opinions. He Ming asked whether she would come to the pilot selection. Only if the time fit her shift and childcare, Wu answered. Her view could be given through the permitted feedback route otherwise. The committee should not require a worker to sacrifice wages in order to prove she valued the service it might provide.

harbor_p26_022.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_022.text: Bao chose a private walk with Dai after the care interval allowed it. They stayed clear of the damaged building and spoke about a new net customer's irritating insistence that knots look decorative. Bao wanted to try another task later if the rate and motion suited. She had the warehouse eighteen and her private work receipts at home, with the continuing care source identified. She did not attend every plan discussion because her recovery had not made her a civic exhibit. Yue met them briefly at the stall and was invited to discuss buns instead, an honor she accepted gladly.

harbor_p26_023.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_023.text: Ke's shears needed ordinary cleaning after the household patch. Tong offered to do it and was given the cloth only after asking how she wanted the blades handled. The tool remained hers. He had begun asking such small questions before acting, which Ke appreciated more than his earlier grand promises to help. Their skiff account and partial claim stayed where the competent process kept them. At the partnership's third batch, she performed the paid checking task under actual hours, with its future acceptance balance still due.

harbor_p26_024.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_024.text: Qin spent a free morning in the garden under his approved shorter role, with his transition covered as actually agreed. He did not carry wage files home to fill the empty hours. A slug had damaged another leaf. He accused it of resisting succession and then laughed alone at how much office language he had brought to beans. The neighbor came to borrow a watering can and returned it at the agreed time. Qin thought about buying another plant with money. The project would earn nothing and delight him if it lived, a respectable bargain he could finally admit making.

harbor_p26_025.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_025.text: At the warehouse, the first ordinary maintenance reply after reopening met its recorded date. The shelf edge was smoothed under the actual task, and the customer received the status through the keeper. Hao inspected the reply rather than interrupt the worker to prove the owner cared. The smaller building was beginning to function inside its confirmed boundary. Her two private closure accounts remained closed, not reserves she could rename in every conversation about need. She met Yue outside and thanked her for the earlier public-route work. The traveler accepted without assuming this gave her a lifelong claim on the place.

harbor_p26_026.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_026.text: Hao asked whether Yue wanted a cart for the journey to the departure stand. Yue thanked her and declined because the habitual pack was light enough and the offer's actual availability would complicate ordinary site work. The owner laughed that every gift she attempted lately met a practical objection. Yue said a private goodbye was available at no cost. They shook hands. The keeper called the owner's next customer question, and she went inside.

harbor_p26_027.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_027.text: Sui prepared the last public pilot presentation with the accepting technical keeper. She would not call the selected work a permanent cure or describe unselected plans as inevitable next budgets. The council's reservation held one sixty-four. Reviews at four and eight weeks belonged to named ordinary roles. Yue's unpaid final presentation would provide a recommendation and identified observations; the committee and keeper would confirm the authorized plan. The captain read the actual agenda, approved the scope within her part and put it down. At home her son's bread recipe waited, unrelated enough to make her want supper.

harbor_p26_028.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_028.text: That evening Han, He Ming and Yue shared food at the clerk's room. The two women argued about road versus registry more affectionately. He Ming said distance made it easy for an office to forget a voice. Han said a route without a receiving desk could bring it back to another empty room. Both were true and neither settled the single fund. Yue asked what would happen to their supper if her recommendation favored repair. They looked at her, then laughed. He Ming said they would criticize her judgment and still pass bread. Han said the criticism might be prolonged.

harbor_p26_029.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_029.text: The next afternoon Yue went to the market for ordinary road food and found two sellers shouting over a basket placed in the wrong receiving space. One called it theft; the other said he had moved it to keep the cart path clear. A child stood between them holding an empty bowl and looking ready to cry. Yue stopped outside the load boundary and asked whose child he was. Both men answered. The argument stalled long enough for them to discover they were pointing to different children, one of whom had already gone home with the actual mother.

harbor_p26_030.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_030.text: The child still there belonged to the noodle seller at the far stall. He had been sent to collect a paid order and had received the bundle during the shouting. The seller came over with the receipt and a face that made both men quieter. She compared the marks, found the noodles under a cloth and gave the neighboring order back. Nobody had stolen a wage chest or hidden a family name. The market had become confused while adults made noise. Yue helped the child carry only his empty bowl back after the seller asked, acquiring no public policing role.

harbor_p26_031.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_031.text: At the noodle stall, the woman insisted on selling Yue a portion rather than give it as reward for ending the argument. The traveler said the seller had ended it and paid the price. She ate seated on a low bench while the child described the terrifying possibility he might bring home vegetables instead of noodles. Yue asked whether vegetables were so alarming. He said his mother had specifically named noodles, which made the distinction morally decisive. She laughed. The hot bowl steamed against cold air, and the market resumed its ordinary noise without recording who had been briefly heroic.

harbor_p26_032.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_032.text: Across the lane a porter dropped a light empty reed tray while clearing space for a larger load. Yue caught it with a hand from the safe side and passed it back when the porter asked. He thanked her and resumed his actual work. The useful motion required no qi, rank or inquiry into private wages. She noticed her own relief at such a small task. A trader nearby asked if she was the harbor cultivator and seemed disappointed by how little light occurred. She offered him the honest explanation that trays generally preferred not to be dropped either way.

harbor_p26_033.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_033.text: He laughed and sold her the ordinary dried food she wanted at the posted private price. She paid from earned money and kept the purchase separate from appointment or pilot funds. The road packet would be used during travel, not appear in the office's loan receipt. At lodging she stored it inside the habitual pack beside her cup and notes. A purchase could be on page without becoming mysterious equipment: food, bought to be eaten. She checked the wrapped pendant remained secure and unspent as fuel, then left again for a private walk with no urgent task waiting.

harbor_p26_034.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_034.text: The walk brought her to the common, where the kite boy sat sulking beside a torn tail tie. He had tried to launch without waiting for the open interval and had been stopped by his mother before entering the cart route. The paper caught a bush instead. He called this injustice. Yue asked whether the bush had read the interval notice. He said bushes should know birthdays had been over for days. She laughed and offered no qi repair. His mother had a private needle and cloth at home. He could mend the tie after carrying the kite safely back.

harbor_p26_035.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_035.text: Fen arrived after work and found the boy still explaining his grievances. She heard three versions of the bush's conduct before asking what actually needed doing. Aning said this was the first sensible question the common had received that afternoon. They went to the household's agreed room with the parent and repaired the tie using its own ordinary materials. The private names on the tail remained mostly unreadable from a distance. The boy now liked that because people who had not been aboard should not announce themselves passengers. The reasoning was nonsense and important to him, so nobody improved it.

harbor_p26_036.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_036.text: Yue watched Fen stitch a small tie and recognized how rarely she now waited for her father to name the next task. Luo had once taught her a knot; now she could teach the boy one ordinary step. When the paper was safely folded, they ate the private bread the parent offered. Aning asked whether Fen would miss her father at the account shop. The girl said she would miss him at supper, which was more exact and hurt more. The others accepted the answer. The household's cat jumped onto an empty stool and declared the conversation finished through occupation.

harbor_p26_037.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_037.text: The cat's claim pleased the boy more than the mended kite. He attempted to appoint it captain and was ignored. Yue laughed until Han arrived at the agreed private hour to collect her for a walk. The clerk admired the repaired tail and asked whether the new captain had accepted ordinary duties. The boy said its consent could be inferred from sitting. Han said this was the worst legal theory she had heard that week, then scratched the animal beneath its chin. The cat accepted the payment and left the stool, disproving the appointment in a way everyone found satisfying.

harbor_p26_038.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_038.text: On the walk, Han asked which room Yue would visit first if she returned someday. The traveler said the one with the actual receiving place she could contact, and the clerk groaned at the answer. Then Yue said her room, if invited and if Han still wanted her there. Han smiled. The direct words embarrassed them less after practice. They passed the renewed window and went farther toward the wall instead of ending at the door. The sea looked cold under the ordinary evening light.

harbor_p26_039.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_039.text: Han said she wanted to keep painting the harbor after the traveler left, even when the figures changed. She might paint the orange curtain's owner one day and would have to admit the cloth had begun to look less offensive. Yue asked whether affection improved color. The clerk said it corrupted criticism. They laughed. Her first future lettering job remained only a possibility with Duan, while the clerk role continued. She had no need to decide the rest of her life because a friend was leaving. The board, room and wages she already had supplied enough work for next week.

harbor_p26_040.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_040.text: At the crew room, Bo requested a training interval for the reporting task he'd watched at the repair demonstration. The employer's lead approved its actual scope inside the current roster, without buying an unselected pilot early. He practiced reading a concern clearly to the named receiving person, then recording its acknowledgment. Deren said the boy's handwriting had improved enough to threaten existing jokes. Bo demanded compensation. Yan told him to accept the competent insult and finish the line. They laughed and checked the current ordinary work, which had no need to wait for a council vote to be done properly.

harbor_p26_041.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_041.text: The technical keeper received the repair launch quotes one last time from the authorized providers. Twenty-eight fittings, sixteen checks, twelve instruction and eight follow-up still totaled sixty-four. None had begun under the reserved fund. The corresponding registry and road quotes were likewise current. The fiscal clerk would check actual work and receipts if selected. Yue heard only the public readiness summary during a private visit permitted for the final presentation. She did not collect tools or acquire inspection authority. The small empty space between approval and purchase had become a place where people could still choose honestly.

harbor_p26_042.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_042.text: The route lead sent Rong the road launch hours, with two collection and two reply journeys over two safe days if selected. The names and six-copper fares belonged to workers. Yue would accompany no trip by default; her volunteer presentation supplied no public ticket. She could help at a shore receiving table if the lead asked and she freely accepted a small task. The plan would still work if she declined. Lu Lian's old message status remained valid whatever the choice. The keeper checked the schedule once, then went to receive a new household question unrelated to the visitor's project.

harbor_p26_043.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_043.text: Han confirmed the registry's cabinet position with Li Su and the walking-stick claimant invited for the check. The funded launch would buy a new twelve-copper cabinet and twelve of forms only if that route was chosen. Demonstration markers returned to ordinary stock afterward. Staff time twenty-four and translation sixteen would pay checked launch tasks, with later four- and eight-week reviews in the accepted desk role. Li read the large-letter sample and asked for one word changed because it could be heard as permission to inspect private files. Han made the correction before anybody had to complain through the cabinet's door.

harbor_p26_044.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_044.text: He Ming came to the clerk's room that evening carrying fruit and her road argument. Han told her arguments cost extra after sunset. The founder paid with an apple and asked whether the cabinet's protected index might actually help the far bank when replies returned. It might, under the permitted receiving arrangement, though it would not pay the journeys. He Ming admitted the plan was better than she had called it at the supper. Han admitted the road was better than she had imagined before hearing Lu Lian's account. Neither changed preference, and the conversation became warmer for that.

harbor_p26_045.speaker: harbor_he_ming
harbor_p26_045.text: I am still going to complain if road loses. I want that said before everybody behaves as if a proper vote requires grateful silence. I can respect the actual decision and keep wanting another service later under a real budget. The fish seller across the water does not become a lesser person because this room gets a cabinet first. And your waiting claimant does not become a fool because I favor a boat. Yue, choose what you can defend from the sources, then allow us to be disappointed without making the disappointment your next employment.

harbor_p26_046.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_046.text: Yue laughed and said nobody had yet offered that employment's bed invoice. Han said the rate would be appalling. The three ate fruit with private tea and argued one more time, now with enough humor to keep the actual differences visible. Sui arrived by invitation carrying a sound loaf she had bought from the baker rather than made. Everyone accused her of withdrawing from the competition. She said ordinary procurement could be wise when three argumentative women required supper. The loaf was good. Her son would receive no report claiming it as a technical achievement of his recipe.

harbor_p26_047.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_047.text: Sui explained that her next supervisory review would fall after the traveler's departure, under the second officer's actual role. Yan's independent signoff conditions likewise continued. Deren's lost earnings were paid and care ongoing, not reopened by a pilot preference. She offered these facts once because the public discussion had blurred them again. Then she refused more work talk and asked Han whether the kite painting could be seen. The clerk showed it privately. Sui identified Qin's cabbage figure at once, which delighted everyone except the absent old man, whose grievance could wait for ordinary time.

harbor_p26_048.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_048.text: Qin heard the artistic judgment the next day and insisted cabbage had greater dignity than most custodians. He was settling into the shorter role with cover and pay, though the habits of long duty still woke him early. He spent the free interval checking beans rather than office drawers. Yue visited by invitation and found the garden disappointing him generously. He offered tea and asked what skill she wanted to learn next. She said making a parcel fold less crooked. He suggested the harbor had trained her in worse matters and could now release her to trivial ambitions with confidence.

harbor_p26_049.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_049.text: Ke completed another actual half-day on the third batch within its two-week schedule. The employer's tools returned to their task keeper at the interval's end. Her own shears cut a household scrap at home, and Tong paid the private tea fee they had jokingly agreed for his sleeve. The venture's reserve remained fourteen; the third balance stayed future money until acceptance in its stated week. He Ming did not ask Yue for capital again. The founders discussed actual future prices among themselves, preserving a business that could survive a friend's refusal without needing the refusal disguised as a later promise.

harbor_p26_050.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_050.text: Wu received her canteen wage at the date and paid the household lease from her own account. The children asked whether Chair the duck should contribute. She said the bird's economic theory consisted of consuming everything and occasionally producing a feather. The neighbor overheard and suggested renting its opinions to the council. Wu laughed and declined because the committee already possessed enough certainty. The room stayed theirs under the private lease. She invited Yue for one more short visit if the departure schedule allowed, then returned to work whose duties left no room for supervising every farewell in the neighborhood.

harbor_p26_051.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_051.text: Bao's care reviewer allowed a longer movement and still limited strenuous work. She wanted to take a future sorting offer from another employer, whose terms had not arrived. Dai helped her phrase the inquiry only after Bao asked. The permitted question went through the ordinary receiving route. Her eighteen paid lost earnings remained hers; the warehouse's two closed private remedies stayed closed. Yue heard the general possibility from Bao at a private stall meeting and asked what she hoped the room would be like. A window that opened, Bao answered, and a supervisor who listened before the ceiling did.

harbor_p26_052.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_052.text: The answer made Dai laugh sadly and Yue go quiet. Bao said she wanted no solemn reaction every time she made a joke about the fire. They apologized in the brief way friends can use and asked about the job inquiry. No answer had arrived yet. They bought another cup of tea and spoke about shirts. The incident had become part of Bao's life without claiming all her available subjects. When the care interval ended, she stood and went home with the cousin who had agreed to accompany her. The traveler waved and did not follow as an unasked observer.

harbor_p26_053.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_053.text: At the last private evening before selection, Yue checked her pack and personal travel papers. The two appointment returns were closed: forty-four from the first, sixteen from the second. The separate maintenance sixty-four remained reserved at its keeper. Emergency sixty-eight and four unused stones remained port stock and cash, not road money. Her own purse had paid fourteen for the private week, plus food and planned ordinary fare. She carried no official file or optional harbor tool. The figures sat still long enough that she could put the notebook away and hear Han knock at the door.

harbor_p26_054.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_054.text: The clerk brought no agenda, just an invitation to walk. Yue accepted. They followed the clear shore road, stopped when an ordinary load passed and resumed after the crew reopened the crossing. Han asked whether the traveler feared the recommendation. She did. The clerk said she feared the goodbye more. The two truths made the silence kinder. They stood at the wall until cold drove them toward private tea. Neither promised what the next six weeks would contain beyond ordinary travel and a contact when a receiving place existed. The road was not yet a room somebody could point to.

harbor_p26_055.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_055.text: Inside, Han read a page of Yue's personal notes only after explicit private permission. It described the day the clerk cried beside the kettle without copying protected household details. Han disliked seeing herself frightened and loved knowing the moment had mattered. She asked the traveler to keep it private. Yue agreed. The book stayed hers, the confidence shared by consent. They closed it before the tea cooled. The clerk's painted board remained on the wall, and the temporary shelf held the notebook for one more visit without pretending it had gained title over the hands that would carry it away.

harbor_p26_056.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_056.text: Yue walked back to lodging late enough that the common was quiet. The kite boy's repaired paper rested indoors, the partnership's gull on its temporary shelf, the office files with ordinary keepers. The three plans had source, keeper, cost and review date. Tomorrow the committee would confirm one after her recommendation. She could speak clearly, let disappointment stay real and then leave with the belongings she brought. At the door she paused to listen to the harbor's night sounds. They had stopped asking her to become a finished answer. She went upstairs, drank water from the familiar cup and slept.

harbor_p26_057.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_057.text: Before sleep, Yue found a grain of salt caught in the fold of her bedding. She shook it into the refuse bowl and watched the speck disappear among larger scraps. It might have come from a storm coat, the fish seller's wrapping or her own careless supper. There was no way to know, and she resisted assigning it a better origin. The cloth smelled faintly of harbor air. She folded it ready for the road, leaving the familiar cup beside the bed. A place could travel with her in such small accidental ways while its tools and papers stayed home.

harbor_p26_058.speaker: narrator
harbor_p26_058.text: Yue slept badly after the conversation, hearing three reasonable plans compete with one purse. She rose for water, used her own cup and looked at the pack already mostly arranged. No official file, stone or loaned tool hid among its habitual contents. Her personal notes could remember the town without carrying its authority. She lay down again and thought of the coming cart, Han's room, Deren's cup and Lu Lian's chosen-name message. The committee would confirm one plan.
